A prior agent black-box probed the jsonschema behavior family "combinators" of the program at /workspace/dataset/test13_executable (usage: /workspace/dataset/test13_executable --a '<instance json>' --b '<schema json>'; prints validator class, True/False, top-level error count).

Its findings were:
---
FILE: /workspace/probes/combinators.jsonl (193 vectors, 16 of them crash cases with exit=1). All outputs captured by running the real binary via node execFileSync.

THE CENTRAL RULE (flatten vs collapse). jsonschema keyword implementations either (a) DESCEND — i.e. `yield from validator.descend(instance, subschema, schema_path=...)`, re-yielding every child error unchanged so each child error becomes its own TOP-LEVEL error; or (b) COLLAPSE — build exactly one ValidationError whose `context` holds the children (context does NOT add to the top-level count). Observed classification:
- DESCEND (flatten, N children => N top-level errors): allOf, then, else, properties, patternProperties, additionalProperties, items, prefixItems, dependentSchemas, dependencies(schema form), $ref, draft-03 `extends`.
- COLLAPSE (always exactly 1 top-level error when it fails, 0 when it passes): anyOf, oneOf, not, contains, draft-03 `disallow`, draft-03 `type` when given an array of schemas.
Flattening composes multiplicatively through descending keywords: `{"items":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0},{"type":"number"}]}}` on `["a","a"]` => 6 errors (3 per item). `{"properties":{"x":{"properties":{"y":{"properties":{"z":{"allOf":[3 failing]}}}}}}}` => 3. But a COLLAPSE keyword anywhere on the path caps the subtree at 1: `{"anyOf":[{"allOf":[2 failing]}]}` => 1; `{"oneOf":[{"allOf":[2 failing]},{"type":"number"}]}` => 1; `{"not":{"anyOf":[...]}}` => 1.

allOf. `{"allOf":[{"type":"number"},{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]}` on "ab" => False/3 (one per failing branch). `{"allOf":[]}` => True/0. `{"allOf":[true,false,false]}` => False/2 (each `false` subschema yields its own top-level error). `{"allOf":[false]}` => False/1. Nested allOf flattens fully: `{"allOf":[{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]},{"type":"number"}]}` => 3. A single allOf branch with multiple failing keywords contributes one error per failing keyword: `{"allOf":[{"properties":{"x":{"type":"number"},"y":{"type":"number"}}},{"properties":{"x":{"minLength":9}}}]}` on {"x":"a","y":"a"} => 3.

anyOf. Fails => exactly 1 error regardless of branch count or of how many errors each branch produced. `{"anyOf":[{"type":"number"},{"minLength":9}]}` => 1. `{"anyOf":[]}` => False/1 (empty anyOf is a FAILURE, unlike empty allOf). `{"anyOf":[false,false]}` => 1. `{"anyOf":[true]}` => True/0. `{"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"number"}]}` => True/0 (short-circuits on first match).

oneOf. Exactly 1 error in both failure modes. 0 matches: `{"oneOf":[{"type":"number"},{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]}` => 1 ("is not valid under any of the given schemas"). 2+ matches: `{"oneOf":[{"type":"string"},{"minLength":1}]}` => 1, `{"oneOf":[true,true]}` => 1, `{"oneOf":[{},{},{}]}` (3 matches) => 1. `{"oneOf":[]}` => False/1. `{"oneOf":[{}]}` => True/0. `{"oneOf":[true,false]}` => True/0.

not. Always exactly 1 error when the subschema matches. `{"not":{"type":"string"}}` on "ab" => 1. `{"not":{}}` => 1. `{"not":true}` => 1. `{"not":false}` => True/0. `{"not":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}}` => True/0 (subschema fails, so not passes). `{"not":{"not":{"type":"number"}}}` => 1. The number of errors the negated subschema would have produced is irrelevant.

if/then/else. Only exists in Draft7, 2019-09, 2020-12. In Draft3/4/6 the keywords `if`, `then`, `else` are COMPLETELY IGNORED (unknown keywords): `{"$schema":draft-06,"if":{"type":"string"},"then":false}` => True/0, while draft-07 => False/1. `then` and `else` DESCEND, so the chosen branch's errors are flattened: `{"if":{"type":"string"},"then":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}}` on "ab" => 2; `{"if":{"type":"number"},"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}}` => 2; on instance 5, `{"if":{"type":"number"},"then":{"minimum":10,"maximum":1,"multipleOf":7}}` => 3. `if` alone (no then/else) never produces an error: `{"if":{"type":"string"}}` => True/0. `then`/`else` WITHOUT `if` are ignored entirely: `{"then":{"minLength":9},"else":{"maxLength":1}}` => True/0 — critically, this means `then`/`else` are NOT standalone keywords; they are only reachable from `if`. Only one branch is evaluated: `{"if":{"type":"string"},"then":true,"else":false}` => True/0. Boolean `if` works: `{"if":true,"then":{"minLength":9}}` => 1; `{"if":false,"else":{"minLength":9}}` => 1. The unused branch is never even looked at, so a MALFORMED unused branch does not crash: `{"if":{"type":"string"},"else":1}` => True/0 and `{"if":{"type":"number"},"then":1}` => True/0, whereas `{"if":{"type":"string"},"then":1}` CRASHES. Nested if/then: `{"if":{"type":"string"},"then":{"if":{"minLength":1},"then":{"maxLength":0,"pattern":"^z"}}}` on "ab" => 2 (inner then flattens through outer then). if/then inside allOf flattens: `{"allOf":[{"if":..,"then":{"minLength":9}},{"if":..,"then":{"maxLength":0}}]}` => 2. if/then inside anyOf/not collapses to 1/0.

DRAFT-03 IS THE BIG SPECIAL CASE. Draft3Validator has NO allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if, then, else — all six are silently ignored. `{"$schema":draft-03,"allOf":[{"type":"number"}],"anyOf":[{"type":"number"}],"oneOf":[],"not":{},"if":{},"then":{"type":"number"}}` on "ab" => True/0. Its analogs instead: `extends` DESCENDS and accepts either a single schema or an array of schemas — `{"extends":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}}` => 2, `{"extends":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]}` => 2. `disallow` COLLAPSES to 1 error (`{"disallow":"string"}` => 1, `{"disallow":["string","number"]}` => 1, `{"disallow":[{"minLength":1}]}` => 1). Draft-03 `type` given an array of subschemas is the anyOf analog and collapses to 1: `{"type":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]}` => 1. `extends` is draft-03 only; in draft-04 `{"extends":{"minLength":9}}` => True/0 (ignored).

Draft-04 through 2020-12 behave IDENTICALLY for allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not, including boolean subschemas (`{"allOf":[true,false,false]}` => 2 even under Draft4Validator, which historically had no boolean schemas). No draft-to-draft count differences were observed anywhere except (a) draft-03's total absence of these keywords and (b) if/then/else being draft-07+.

RELATED CONDITIONAL KEYWORDS. `dependentSchemas` (2019-09+) DESCENDS: `{"dependentSchemas":{"a":{"minProperties":9,"maxProperties":0}}}` on {"a":1} => 2. Draft-07 `dependencies` with a schema value likewise DESCENDS => 2. `contains` COLLAPSES: `{"contains":{"type":"string"}}` on [1,2] => 1. In 2019-09, `if`/`then` and `anyOf` DO contribute annotations for `unevaluatedProperties`: `{"properties":{"a":{}},"if":{"properties":{"a":{}}},"then":{"properties":{"b":{}}},"unevaluatedProperties":false}` on {"a":1,"b":2} => True/0, and `{"anyOf":[{"properties":{"b":{}}}],"properties":{"a":{}},"unevaluatedProperties":false}` => True/0, while dropping the combinator gives False/1.

SIBLING KEYWORDS ADD INDEPENDENTLY. Errors from combinators sum with sibling keyword errors at the same level: `{"type":"number","allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}` on "ab" => 3; `{"minLength":9,"allOf":[{"maxLength":0}],"anyOf":[{"type":"number"}],"oneOf":[],"not":{}}` => 5 (1 minLength + 1 allOf-descended + 1 anyOf + 1 oneOf + 1 not). `{"anyOf":[{"type":"string"}],"minLength":9}` => 1 (anyOf passes, minLength fails).

$ref is transparent to counting: `{"$ref":"#/$defs/a","$defs":{"a":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}}}` => 2, and `{"allOf":[{"$ref":"#/$defs/a"}],"$defs":{"a":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}}}` => 2.

CRASH BEHAVIOR (exit code 1, Python traceback on stderr, NOTHING on stdout — the three print lines never execute because is_valid() raises first). Observed crashes, all with exit=1:
- Non-list values for allOf/anyOf/oneOf whose iteration yields non-dict/non-bool elements: `{"allOf":{"type":"number"}}`, `{"anyOf":{"type":"number"}}`, `{"oneOf":{"a":{"type":"number"}}}` (dict iterates to its string keys), `{"oneOf":"x"}`, `{"allOf":"ab"}` (string iterates to chars) => AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get' at referencing/jsonschema.py _dollar_id.
- Non-iterable values: `{"allOf":0}`, `{"allOf":null}`, `{"anyOf":true}` => exit 1 (TypeError, not iterable).
- Non-schema ELEMENTS: `{"allOf":[null]}` => AttributeError 'NoneType' has no attribute 'get'; `{"allOf":[1]}` => 'int' object has no attribute 'get'; `{"anyOf":[null]}` same.
- `not` with a non-dict/non-bool: `{"not":[{"type":"number"}]}` => AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'items' (in Validator.__attrs_post_init__); `{"not":null}` / `{"not":1}` => TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType'/'int' is not iterable (in validator_for).
- `{"if":1,"then":{...}}` => TypeError not iterable (validator_for, evaluating `if`); `{"if":{"type":"string"},"then":1}` => AttributeError 'int' has no attribute 'get' (descend into `then`) — but only when the branch is actually taken.
NOT crashes (empty iterables): `{"allOf":""}` => True/0, `{"allOf":{}}` => True/0 (zero subschemas => vacuously valid), while `{"anyOf":""}`, `{"anyOf":{}}`, `{"oneOf":{}}` => False/1 (zero subschemas => nothing matched).
---
Gotchas it listed: ["allOf DESCENDS (N failing branches => N top-level errors, and each branch's own multiple keyword failures each count too), while anyOf/oneOf/not/contains COLLAPSE to exactly 1 error with children in .context. Implementers who make all combinators collapse (or all flatten) get counts wrong everywhere.","Empty combinator arrays diverge: {\"allOf\":[]} => valid/0 errors, but {\"anyOf\":[]} and {\"oneOf\":[]} => INVALID with exactly 1 error.","oneOf yields exactly 1 error for BOTH failure modes: 0 matches and 2+ matches (even 3 matches => 1). Do not emit one error per extra match.","then/else DESCEND, so a then-branch with 3 failing keywords produces 3 TOP-LEVEL errors, not 1. This is the most commonly mis-implemented count.","then and else without a sibling `if` are completely ignored (0 errors) — they are not standalone keywords; the if_ handler is the only thing that reaches them.","`if` alone (no then/else) never produces an error, even when it fails. It is only an annotation/selector.","if/then/else do NOT exist before draft-07. Draft3/4/6 silently ignore them; {\"$schema\":draft-06,\"if\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"then\":false} is VALID while draft-07 gives 1 error.","Draft-03 has NONE of allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not/if/then/else — all are ignored, so a schema of pure combinators is vacuously valid under Draft3Validator. Its analogs are `extends` (descends, accepts schema or array of schemas), `disallow` (collapses to 1), and `type` with an array containing subschemas (collapses to 1). `extends` is ignored in draft-04+.","Boolean subschemas work inside combinators in EVERY draft including draft-04: {\"allOf\":[true,false,false]} => 2 errors under Draft4Validator. Don't gate boolean subschema support on draft>=6.","{\"not\":false} is VALID (0 errors) and {\"not\":true} / {\"not\":{}} are INVALID (1 error) — easy to invert.","A collapsing keyword anywhere on the path caps the whole subtree at 1 error: {\"anyOf\":[{\"allOf\":[2 failing]}]} => 1, not 2. Flattening only multiplies through chains of descending keywords (properties/items/prefixItems/allOf/then/else/$ref/dependentSchemas).","Malformed combinator values CRASH with exit=1 and NO stdout at all (not even the validator class name), because is_valid() raises before the prints. Distinguish: {\"allOf\":\"\"} and {\"allOf\":{}} do NOT crash (empty iteration => valid), {\"allOf\":\"ab\"} and {\"allOf\":{\"type\":\"number\"}} DO crash (iterating a str/dict yields strings, which are not schemas), and {\"allOf\":0}/{\"allOf\":null}/{\"anyOf\":true} crash as non-iterable.","`if`/`then`/`else` are evaluated lazily: a malformed UNTAKEN branch does not crash. {\"if\":{\"type\":\"number\"},\"then\":1} on a string is VALID/0, but {\"if\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"then\":1} on a string CRASHES.","Combinator errors sum with sibling keyword errors at the same schema level; there is no short-circuiting between keywords.","In 2019-09+, if/then and anyOf branches DO contribute successful-property annotations consumed by unevaluatedProperties, so a passing combinator branch can make unevaluatedProperties:false pass."]
Its vectors are in /workspace/probes/combinators.jsonl (193 lines of JSONL, each {"a","b","out","exit"}).

You are the COMPLETENESS CRITIC. Its assignment was:
Boolean combinators and conditionals.
Probe: allOf (3 failing branches => how many top-level errors? likely 3 since allOf descends), anyOf (all failing => 1 error with context), oneOf (0 matches => 1 error; 2+ matches => 1 error), not (=> 1 error), if/then/else (draft7+; ignored in draft6/4/3?), if with no then/else, if-then-else nesting, error counts when then-branch has multiple failures (does it produce N top-level errors or 1?).
Also: allOf containing properties that fail multiple times; combinators nested inside properties (count bubbling); empty allOf/anyOf/oneOf arrays; allOf with boolean schemas (true/false); 'not': true / 'not': false; combinator value not an array (crash?).
Determine precisely the RULE for when sub-errors are flattened into top-level errors vs collapsed into one error with context. Test deeply nested: {"properties":{"x":{"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"minLength":9}]}}} with x=1.

Root schema `true` -> True/0; root `false` -> False/1.

THE CENTRAL RULE (DESCEND vs COLLAPSE). A keyword implementation either (a) DESCENDs -- `yield from validator.descend(...)`, so every child error is re-yielded and becomes its OWN top-level error -- or (b) COLLAPSEs -- builds exactly one ValidationError whose children go into `.context`, which does NOT add to the top-level count. Measured classification (each tested with a 2-failing-keyword subschema {"minLength":9,"maxLength":0} against "ab"):
  DESCEND: allOf, then, else, properties, patternProperties, additionalProperties (ONLY when the value is a schema object), items (draft-04..2019-09 single-schema form, and 2020-12 schema form), prefixItems, additionalItems (draft-07 schema form), propertyNames, dependentSchemas, dependencies (schema form), $ref, draft-03 `extends`.
  COLLAPSE (always exactly 1 error when failing, 0 when passing): anyOf, oneOf, not, contains, minContains/maxContains, draft-03 `disallow`, draft-03 `type` when given an array.
  PER-ITEM-BUT-NOT-DESCENDING (fixed counts that are neither): `required` yields ONE error PER missing property ({} vs {"required":["a","b","c"]} => 3; duplicates count separately, {"required":["a","a"]} => 2); `dependentRequired`/draft<=7 `dependencies` array form yields one error per missing dependency ({"a":1} vs {"dependencies":{"a":["b","c"]}} => 2); `additionalProperties: false` yields exactly ONE aggregate error no matter how many extras (2 extras => 1, 3 extras => 1); 2020-12 `items: false` yields exactly ONE aggregate error for all extras ([1,2] => 1, [1,2,3] with prefixItems:[{}] => 1); draft-07 `additionalItems: false` also 1.
  DESCEND multiplies: {"items":{"allOf":[3 failing]}} on ["a","a","a"] => 9. {"items":{"items":{"allOf":[2 failing]}}} on [["a","a"],["a","a"]] => 8. {"propertyNames":{"allOf":[{"maxLength":0},{"pattern":"^z"}]}} on {"a":"x","b":"y"} => 4. Three levels of nested properties + allOf of 3 => 3.
  A COLLAPSE keyword ANYWHERE on the path caps that whole subtree at 1: {"anyOf":[{"allOf":[2 failing]}]} => 1; {"items":{"anyOf":[{"allOf":[2]}]}} on ["a"] => 1; {"properties":{"x":{"anyOf":[deep 2-failing tree]}}} => 1; {"contains":{"allOf":[2]}} => 1; {"not":{"anyOf":[...]}} => 1. Above a collapse point, counting resumes normally: {"items":{"oneOf":[{"minLength":9}]}} on ["a","a"] => 2 (1 per item).
  Siblings SUM, no short-circuiting between keywords: {"minLength":9,"maxLength":0,"pattern":"^z","type":"number","allOf":[{"minLength":9}],"anyOf":[{"type":"number"}],"oneOf":[],"not":{},"enum":["q"],"const":"q"} on "ab" => 10. {"type":"array","required":["b","c"],"minProperties":5,"allOf":[{"maxProperties":0}],"not":{}} on {"a":1} => 6. Key order in the schema object does not change the count.

allOf. {"allOf":[{"type":"number"},{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]} on "ab" => False/3. {"allOf":[]} => True/0. {"allOf":[true,true]} => True/0. {"allOf":[true,false,false]} => False/2. {"allOf":[false]} => 1. Nested allOf flattens fully (allOf of allOf of 2 plus one more => 3). One branch with several failing keywords contributes one error per keyword. allOf does NOT short-circuit: a malformed later element always crashes.

anyOf. Fails => exactly 1 error, independent of branch count or of how many errors branches produced. {"anyOf":[]} => False/1 (UNLIKE allOf). {"anyOf":[false,false]} => 1. {"anyOf":[true]} => True/0. Triple-nested anyOf of a failing schema => 1. Two sibling anyOfs each failing => 2 (each contributes its own single error). anyOf SHORT-CIRCUITS on the first matching branch: {"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},null]} is True/0 on "a" but CRASHES on 1; {"anyOf":[true,null]} => True/0.

oneOf. Exactly 1 error in BOTH failure modes. Zero matches: 1. Two or more matches: 1 -- even with 3 matches ({"oneOf":[{},{},{}]} => 1, {"oneOf":[{"type":"number"},{"type":"string"},{"minLength":1},{"maxLength":9}]} on "a" => 1). {"oneOf":[]} => False/1. {"oneOf":[{}]} => True/0. {"oneOf":[true,false]} => True/0. {"oneOf":[false,false,false]} => 1. Exactly one match anywhere in the list (first, middle, or last) => True/0. oneOf does NOT short-circuit -- after finding the first match it still evaluates every remaining branch to detect extra matches, so {"oneOf":[{"type":"string"},null]} CRASHES on "a" while the anyOf equivalent does not. This asymmetry is the single sharpest anyOf/oneOf behavioural difference.

not. Exactly 1 error when the subschema matches; the negated subschema's own error count is irrelevant. {"not":{"type":"string"}} on "ab" => 1. {"not":{}} => 1. {"not":true} => 1. {"not":false} => True/0. {"not":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}} => True/0. {"not":{"not":{}}} => True/0; {"not":{"not":{"not":{}}}} => 1. {"allOf":[{"not":{}},{"not":{}}]} => 2. {"oneOf":[{"not":{}},{"not":{}}]} => 1. `not` does NOT contribute annotations for unevaluatedProperties.

if/then/else. Present ONLY in Draft7, 2019-09, 2020-12. Draft3/4/6 treat if/then/else as unknown keywords and IGNORE them entirely ({"$schema":draft-06,"if":{"type":"string"},"then":false} => True/0; draft-07 => False/1). `then` and `else` DESCEND: {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}} on "ab" => 2; {"if":{"type":"number"},"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}} => 2; on 5, {"if":{"type":"number"},"then":{"minimum":10,"maximum":1,"multipleOf":7}} => 3; an else branch with 3 failing keywords => 3. `if` ALONE never produces an error even when it fails -- it is purely a selector. `then`/`else` WITHOUT a sibling `if` are ignored completely ({"then":false} => True/0, {"else":false} => True/0); the if_ handler is the only code path that reaches them. Exactly one branch runs: {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":true,"else":false} => True/0. Boolean `if` works: {"if":true,"then":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}} => 2; {"if":false,"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}} => 2; {"if":{}} behaves like true. Evaluation is LAZY -- an untaken malformed branch never crashes: {"if":{"type":"number"},"then":null} on "a" => True/0 and {"if":{"type":"string"},"else":null} => True/0, but {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":null} and {"if":{"type":"number"},"else":null} CRASH. Combinators inside `if` work and their errors are discarded: {"if":{"anyOf":[{"type":"number"}]},"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}} => 2; {"if":{"not":{}},"then":{"minLength":9},"else":{"maxLength":0,"pattern":"^z"}} => 2. In Draft4/6/7, keywords SIBLING to `$ref` are IGNORED: {"$ref":"#/definitions/a","minLength":9,"maxLength":0,"definitions":{"a":{"pattern":"^z","type":"string"}}} on "ab" => 1 (only the ref's own pattern error). Recursive $ref works. unevaluatedProperties / unevaluatedItems (2019-09+; IGNORED in draft-07 and earlier: {"properties":{"a":{}},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1,"b":2} => True/0 under draft-07, False/1 under 2019-09). unevaluatedProperties yields exactly ONE aggregate error regardless of how many properties are unevaluated (1 extra => 1, 2 extras => 1). PER-DRAFT KEYWORD AVAILABILITY (a keyword absent from a draft is silently ignored => 0 errors). allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not: draft-04 and up. if/then/else: draft-07 and up. `dependencies`: draft-03 through draft-07 ONLY -- REMOVED in 2019-09/2020-12, where {"dependencies":{"a":["b","c"]}} on {"a":1} => True/0 while draft-03/4/6/7 give 2. `dependentSchemas`/`dependentRequired`: 2019-09+ only (=> 2 there, 0 in draft<=7). `contains`: draft-06+ (draft-03/04 ignore it). `minContains`/`maxContains`: 2019-09+ (draft-07 ignores them, so {"contains":{"type":"number"},"maxContains":1} on [1,2,3] => True/0 in draft-07 but False/1 in 2019-09+). `propertyNames`: draft-06+ (=> 2 errors for a 2-failing subschema; draft-03/04 => 0). `const`: draft-06+. `prefixItems`: 2020-12 ONLY -- in every earlier draft it is an unknown keyword (=> 0), so {"prefixItems":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"string"}]} on [1,2] is True/0 for draft-03..2019-09 and False/2 for 2020-12. `items` as an ARRAY (tuple form) plus `additionalItems`: draft-04..draft-07 (2020-12 uses prefixItems + items). `items: false` on [1,2]: draft-07 DESCENDS per item => 2 errors; 2020-12 emits ONE aggregate error => 1. Boolean subschemas work inside combinators in EVERY draft including draft-04 ({"allOf":[true,false,false]} => 2 under Draft4Validator). Aside from the availability differences listed here and the $ref-sibling rule, draft-04 through 2020-12 behave identically for allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not counting.

DRAFT-03 (the big special case). Draft3Validator has NO allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if, then, else, const, contains, propertyNames, prefixItems, dependentSchemas, dependentRequired -- all silently ignored, so a schema of pure combinators is vacuously valid. Its analogs: `extends` DESCENDS and accepts a single schema OR an array of schemas ({"extends":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}} => 2; {"extends":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1},{"type":"number"}]} => 3; nested {"extends":{"extends":{...2 failing}}} => 2; {"extends":[{"extends":{"minLength":9}},{"maxLength":1}]} => 2; {"extends":[]} => True/0; {"extends":{}} => True/0; {"extends":true} CRASHES). `disallow` COLLAPSES to exactly 1 ({"disallow":"string"} => 1, {"disallow":"any"} => 1, {"disallow":["string","number"]} => 1, {"disallow":[{"type":"object"}]} on {} => 1) and PASSES when its subschemas fail ({"disallow":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]} on "ab" => True/0); {"disallow":[]} => True/0. Draft-03 `type` given an array is the anyOf analog and COLLAPSES to 1 ({"type":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]} => 1; {"type":[]} => 1; mixed strings and schemas work: {"type":[{"minLength":1},"number"]} => True/0, {"type":["number",{"minLength":9}]} => 1). Draft-03 `required` is a BOOLEAN inside each property schema, one error per missing required property ({"properties":{"a":{"required":true},"b":{"required":true}}} on {} => 2), and combines with extends ({"properties":{"a":{"required":true}},"extends":{"properties":{"b":{"required":true}}}} => 2). Draft-03 IGNORES draft-04-style {"required":["a","b"]} => True/0. `divisibleBy` is draft-03's multipleOf => 1. `extends` is draft-03 ONLY -- draft-04/06/07/2020-12 ignore it => True/0.

JAVASCRIPT-REIMPLEMENTER TRAPS (Python semantics leaking through). (1) STRING LENGTH IS CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 units: "𝄞" (U+1D11E) has length 1, so {"allOf":[{"maxLength":1}]} => True/0 and {"allOf":[{"minLength":2}]} => 1; "😀😀" has length 2 so {"maxLength":2} passes; a JS `.length` implementation gets all of these backwards. But combining marks DO count separately: "é" has length 2, so {"maxLength":1} => 1 error. `{"propertyNames":{"allOf":[{"maxLength":1}]}}` on {"<emoji>":1} => True/0. (2) REGEX IS PYTHON `re.search`, NOT JS RegExp: `pattern` is a SEARCH not a full match ({"pattern":"b"} on "abc" => valid, {"pattern":"^b"} => 1). Python `$` matches BEFORE a trailing newline, so {"pattern":"^a$"} on "a\n" => True/0 (JS would fail) and {"not":{"pattern":"^a$"}} on "a\n" => 1. `\d` and `\w` are UNICODE-aware: "٣" (Arabic-Indic three) matches "^\\d$" => True/0, "é" matches "^\\w$" => True/0. Python-only syntax works: inline flags `(?i)abc` matches "ABC"; `\Z` is supported; named groups `(?P<x>a)` are supported -- all three THROW in JS RegExp. `.` matches an astral char as one unit: "^.$" matches an emoji => True/0. An INVALID regex like `{"pattern":"["}` CRASHES (exit 1). Overlapping patternProperties both apply: {"patternProperties":{"^a":{"type":"number"},"X$":{"type":"number"}}} on {"aX":"s","aY":"s"} => 3. (3) BOOLEANS ARE NOT NUMBERS despite Python's bool<:int -- jsonschema unbools explicitly: `true` is neither "integer" nor "number" (=> 1 error each); {"oneOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"boolean"}]} => True/0 for both `true` and `1`; {"enum":[1]} rejects `true` and {"enum":[true]} rejects `1`; {"const":1} rejects `true` and {"const":true} rejects `1`; {"const":[true]} rejects `[1]`; uniqueItems treats them as DISTINCT ([true,1] unique, [0,false] unique, but [1,1.0,true] => 1 error because 1 and 1.0 collide). (4) 1 vs 1.0: numerically EQUAL for const/enum/uniqueItems ({"oneOf":[{"const":1},{"const":1.0}]} => 1 error from TWO matches for both instance 1 and instance 1.0; {"oneOf":[{"const":1e2},{"const":100}]} on 100 => 1; [1,1.0] fails uniqueItems; {"const":{"a":1.0}} matches {"a":1}). But `type: "integer"` DIFFERS BY DRAFT: 1.0 is NOT an integer in draft-03/draft-04 but IS in draft-06+ (so {"oneOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"number"}]} on 1.0 => True/0 in draft-04 and False/1 in draft-06+ -- an actual validity flip). -0.0 and 1e2 are integers in draft-06+. (5) -0: JSON `-0` parses to Python int 0, so {"const":-0} matches 0, {"oneOf":[{"const":0},{"const":-0}]} => 1 error (two matches), and [0,-0] FAILS uniqueItems. (6) FLOAT PRECISION: multipleOf uses float division, so {"multipleOf":0.1} on 0.3 FAILS (1 error) while {"multipleOf":0.0001} on 0.0075 and {"multipleOf":1.5} on 4.5 pass; {"multipleOf":1e-308} on 1e308 fails (overflow). Arbitrary-precision integers work: 12345678901234567890123 satisfies {"type":"integer"} and {"multipleOf":1}. `1e400` parses to float inf and satisfies {"type":"number"}. (7) OBJECT KEYS: duplicate JSON keys -> LAST wins ({"a":1,"a":2} matches {"properties":{"a":{"const":2}}}). Key insertion order never changes error COUNTS. Deep equality is order-insensitive for objects ({"const":{"b":2,"a":1}} matches {"a":1,"b":2}) but order-SENSITIVE for arrays ({"enum":[[2,1],[1,2]]} matches [1,2] via the second entry only). (8) TYPE-INAPPLICABLE KEYWORDS ARE NO-OPS, which silently reduces counts: {"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0},{"pattern":"^z"}]} on the NUMBER 1 => True/0; {"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"minItems":9},{"maxItems":0}]} on [1,2,3] => 2 (minLength skipped); {"properties":{"x":{"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"minLength":9}]}}} with x=1 => ONE error, not two. (9) `format` is NOT asserted by default: {"allOf":[{"format":"email"},{"format":"date"}]} on "zz" => True/0. (10) Unknown keywords and `$comment` are ignored without error.

contains DETAIL. Collapses to 1. Empty array with any contains => 1. {"contains":false} on [] => 1 (and on any array). {"contains":true} on [1] => True/0. A NON-ARRAY instance makes contains a no-op ({"contains":{"type":"number"}} on "a" => True/0). minContains/maxContains each add their own single error when violated ([1,2,3] with maxContains:1 => 1; with minContains:5 => 1; with minContains:2,maxContains:2 => 1). {"contains":{"type":"number"},"minContains":0} on [] => True/0. contains and a sibling items both fire: {"contains":{allOf 2 failing},"items":{allOf 2 failing}} on ["a","a"] => 5 (1 + 4).

CRASH MATRIX (exit=1, empty stdout). For allOf/anyOf/oneOf the value is iterated and each element passed to the schema machinery. NON-CRASHING degenerate values are exactly the EMPTY ITERABLES: `""` and `{}` -- {"allOf":""} and {"allOf":{}} => True/0 (vacuous), while {"anyOf":""}, {"anyOf":{}}, {"oneOf":""}, {"oneOf":{}} => False/1 (nothing matched), mirroring the empty-array results {"allOf":[]} => True/0 vs {"anyOf":[]}/{"oneOf":[]} => False/1. EVERYTHING ELSE CRASHES: non-empty strings ({"allOf":"x"}, {"allOf":"ab"} -- iterating yields chars, AttributeError 'str' has no attribute 'get'), non-empty objects ({"allOf":{"type":"number"}}, {"allOf":{"a":{...}}}, {"allOf":{"":{}}} -- iterating yields keys), and all non-iterables (0, 1.5, null, true, false). Because anyOf short-circuits, a bad element AFTER a matching branch is never reached (no crash); oneOf always scans the rest, so it always crashes. Other crashes: {"pattern":"["} (invalid regex), {"$schema":7}, draft-03 {"extends":true}, unresolvable $ref pointers (including inside anyOf), remote http $ref, and 2019-09 $recursiveRef without $id. `pattern` is Python `re.search`, not JS RegExp: unanchored by default; `$` matches before a trailing newline so "a\n" MATCHES "^a$"; `\d` and `\w` are Unicode-aware (Arabic-Indic digits match \d); Python-only syntax `(?i)`, `\Z`, `(?P<name>...)` all work. An invalid regex like "[" CRASHES with exit=1.

Booleans are never numbers: `true` fails type integer AND type number; {"enum":[1]} rejects true, {"const":true} rejects 1, and uniqueItems treats [true,1] and [0,false] as UNIQUE. But 1 and 1.0 ARE equal for const/enum/uniqueItems ([1,1.0] fails uniqueItems, {"oneOf":[{"const":1},{"const":1.0}]} => 1 error from two matches), and -0 equals 0 ([0,-0] fails uniqueItems).

`type: "integer"` on 1.0 is FALSE in draft-03/draft-04 but TRUE in draft-06+ -- a real validity flip, e.g. {"oneOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"number"}]} on 1.0 is VALID in draft-04 and INVALID (1 error) in draft-06+.
multipleOf uses float arithmetic: {"multipleOf":0.1} on 0.3 FAILS. Don't 'fix' it with epsilon rounding.

Keywords that don't apply to the instance's type are silent no-ops, which quietly reduces counts. The assignment's own vector {"properties":{"x":{"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"minLength":9}]}}} with x=1 gives ONE error, not two, because minLength ignores numbers.

In 2019-09+, successful allOf/anyOf/oneOf/if-then/if-else branches DO contribute property annotations that satisfy unevaluatedProperties (making it pass), but `not` does NOT. unevaluatedProperties/unevaluatedItems emit exactly ONE aggregate error regardless of how many members are unevaluated, and are entirely ignored in draft-07 and earlier.

`not` polarity: {"not":false} is VALID/0 while {"not":true} and {"not":{}} are INVALID/1. And {"not":[]} / {"not":""} CRASH even though they look 'empty' -- unlike allOf/anyOf, `not` requires a dict or bool.

`required` emits one error PER missing property (3 missing => 3, and duplicate entries in the list count twice), unlike additionalProperties:false which aggregates. dependentRequired and draft<=7 array-form dependencies likewise emit one per missing dependency.

Crashes print NOTHING on stdout (not even the validator class name) and exit 1, because is_valid() raises before the first print. Unresolvable $ref pointers crash even when wrapped in anyOf -- anyOf does not swallow resolution errors, only validation errors.

Draft-03 has NONE of allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not/if/then/else/const/contains/propertyNames/prefixItems, so a pure-combinator schema is vacuously valid. Its analogs: `extends` (DESCENDS, schema or array of schemas, but {"extends":true} CRASHES), `disallow` (COLLAPSES to 1, and PASSES when its subschemas fail), array-valued `type` (COLLAPSES to 1, mixes type-name strings and subschemas), boolean `required` inside each property schema (draft-04-style {"required":[...]} is IGNORED), `divisibleBy`. `extends` is ignored in draft-04+.

THE CENTRAL RULE (DESCEND vs COLLAPSE). A keyword either (a) DESCENDs -- yield from validator.descend(...), so every child error is re-yielded and becomes its OWN top-level error -- or (b) COLLAPSEs -- builds exactly one ValidationError whose children go into .context, which does NOT add to the top-level count. Measured classification (each tested with a 2-failing-keyword subschema {"minLength":9,"maxLength":0} against "ab"):
  DESCEND: allOf, then, else, properties, patternProperties, additionalProperties (ONLY when the value is a schema object), items (draft-04..2019-09 single-schema form, and 2020-12 schema form), prefixItems, additionalItems (draft-07 schema form), propertyNames, dependentSchemas, dependencies (schema form), $ref, draft-03 extends.
  COLLAPSE (exactly 1 error when failing, 0 when passing): anyOf, oneOf, not, contains, minContains/maxContains, draft-03 disallow, draft-03 type when given an array.
  NEITHER (fixed per-item counts): required yields ONE error PER missing property ({} vs {"required":["a","b","c"]} => 3; duplicates count separately, {"required":["a","a"]} => 2). dependentRequired and draft<=7 array-form dependencies yield one error per missing dependency ({"a":1} vs {"dependencies":{"a":["b","c"]}} => 2). additionalProperties:false yields exactly ONE aggregate error no matter how many extras (2 extras => 1, 3 extras => 1). 2020-12 items:false yields exactly ONE aggregate error for all extras ([1,2] => 1; [1,2,3] with prefixItems:[{}] => 1). draft-07 additionalItems:false also 1.
  DESCEND multiplies: {"items":{"allOf":[3 failing]}} on ["a","a","a"] => 9. {"items":{"items":{"allOf":[2 failing]}}} on [["a","a"],["a","a"]] => 8. {"propertyNames":{"allOf":[{"maxLength":0},{"pattern":"^z"}]}} on {"a":"x","b":"y"} => 4. Three nested properties levels + allOf of 3 => 3. {"properties":{"a":{allOf 2},"b":{allOf 2}}} => 4.
  A COLLAPSE keyword ANYWHERE on the path caps that subtree at 1: {"anyOf":[{"allOf":[2 failing]}]} => 1; {"items":{"anyOf":[{"allOf":[2]}]}} on ["a"] => 1; {"properties":{"x":{"anyOf":[deep 2-failing tree]}}} => 1; {"contains":{"allOf":[2]}} => 1; {"not":{"anyOf":[...]}} => 1. Above a collapse point counting resumes: {"items":{"oneOf":[{"minLength":9}]}} on ["a","a"] => 2.
  Siblings SUM, no short-circuiting between keywords: {"minLength":9,"maxLength":0,"pattern":"^z","type":"number","allOf":[{"minLength":9}],"anyOf":[{"type":"number"}],"oneOf":[],"not":{},"enum":["q"],"const":"q"} on "ab" => 10. {"type":"array","required":["b","c"],"minProperties":5,"allOf":[{"maxProperties":0}],"not":{}} on {"a":1} => 6. Schema key order never changes counts.

allOf. {"allOf":[{"type":"number"},{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]} on "ab" => False/3. {"allOf":[]} => True/0. {"allOf":[true,true]} => True/0. {"allOf":[true,false,false]} => False/2. {"allOf":[false]} => 1. Nested allOf flattens fully. One branch with several failing keywords contributes one error per keyword. allOf never short-circuits: a malformed later element always crashes.

anyOf. Fails => exactly 1 error regardless of branch count or child error counts. {"anyOf":[]} => False/1 (UNLIKE allOf). {"anyOf":[false,false]} => 1. {"anyOf":[true]} => True/0. Triple-nested anyOf of a failing schema => 1. Two sibling anyOfs each failing => 2. anyOf SHORT-CIRCUITS on the first matching branch: {"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},null]} is True/0 on "a" but CRASHES on 1; {"anyOf":[true,null]} => True/0.

oneOf. Exactly 1 error in BOTH failure modes. Zero matches: 1. Two or more matches: 1 -- even 3 matches ({"oneOf":[{},{},{}]} => 1; {"oneOf":[{"type":"number"},{"type":"string"},{"minLength":1},{"maxLength":9}]} on "a" => 1). {"oneOf":[]} => False/1. {"oneOf":[{}]} => True/0. {"oneOf":[true,false]} => True/0. {"oneOf":[false,false,false]} => 1. Exactly one match anywhere in the list (first, middle, or last) => True/0. oneOf does NOT short-circuit -- after the first match it still evaluates every remaining branch to count extra matches, so {"oneOf":[{"type":"string"},null]} CRASHES on "a" while the anyOf equivalent does not. This is the sharpest anyOf/oneOf behavioural difference.

not. Exactly 1 error when the subschema matches; the negated subschema's own error count is irrelevant. {"not":{"type":"string"}} on "ab" => 1. {"not":{}} => 1. {"not":true} => 1. {"not":false} => True/0. {"not":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}} => True/0. {"not":{"not":{}}} => True/0; {"not":{"not":{"not":{}}}} => 1. {"allOf":[{"not":{}},{"not":{}}]} => 2. {"oneOf":[{"not":{}},{"not":{}}]} => 1. not does NOT contribute annotations for unevaluatedProperties.

if/then/else. Present ONLY in Draft7, 2019-09, 2020-12. Draft3/4/6 treat if/then/else as unknown keywords and IGNORE them ({"$schema":draft-06,"if":{"type":"string"},"then":false} => True/0; draft-07 => False/1). then and else DESCEND: {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}} on "ab" => 2; {"if":{"type":"number"},"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}} => 2; on 5, {"if":{"type":"number"},"then":{"minimum":10,"maximum":1,"multipleOf":7}} => 3; an else branch with 3 failing keywords => 3. if ALONE never produces an error even when it fails -- purely a selector. then/else WITHOUT a sibling if are ignored completely ({"then":false} => True/0, {"else":false} => True/0); the if_ handler is the only path that reaches them. Exactly one branch runs: {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":true,"else":false} => True/0. Boolean if works: {"if":true,"then":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}} => 2; {"if":false,"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}} => 2; {"if":{}} behaves like true. Evaluation is LAZY -- an untaken malformed branch never crashes: {"if":{"type":"number"},"then":null} on "a" => True/0 and {"if":{"type":"string"},"else":null} => True/0, but {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":null} and {"if":{"type":"number"},"else":null} CRASH. Combinators inside if work and their errors are discarded: {"if":{"anyOf":[{"type":"number"}]},"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}} => 2; {"if":{"not":{}},"then":{"minLength":9},"else":{"maxLength":0,"pattern":"^z"}} => 2. Nesting: if/then inside allOf flattens (2); inside anyOf => 1; inside not => 0/1.

$ref AND SIBLING KEYWORDS -- BIGGEST CROSS-DRAFT COUNT DIFFERENCE (missed entirely by the prior report). In Draft4/6/7, keywords SIBLING to $ref are IGNORED: {"$ref":"#/definitions/a","minLength":9,"maxLength":0,"definitions":{"a":{"pattern":"^z","type":"string"}}} on "ab" => 1 (only the ref's own pattern error). The IDENTICAL schema under 2019-09/2020-12 with $defs => 3. Same inside allOf: {"allOf":[{"$ref":"#/X/a","minLength":9}],"X":{"a":{"maxLength":0}}} => 1 under draft-4/6/7, 2 under 2019-09/2020-12. With no siblings, $ref is transparent to counting in every draft: {"$ref":"#/$defs/a","$defs":{"a":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}}} => 2, and a $ref reached through nested properties still flattens => 2. Recursive $ref works. An UNRESOLVABLE pointer CRASHES even inside anyOf ({"anyOf":[{"$ref":"#/$defs/missing"}]} crashes -- anyOf does NOT swallow resolution failures); a remote http $ref crashes (no network resolver). 2020-12 $dynamicRef/$dynamicAnchor resolves normally; a 2019-09 $recursiveRef/$recursiveAnchor schema without $id CRASHES.

unevaluatedProperties / unevaluatedItems (2019-09+; IGNORED in draft-07 and earlier: {"properties":{"a":{}},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1,"b":2} => True/0 under draft-07, False/1 under 2019-09). unevaluatedProperties yields exactly ONE aggregate error regardless of how many properties are unevaluated (1 extra => 1, 2 extras => 1). Successful if/then, anyOf, oneOf, and allOf branches DO contribute property annotations that satisfy it: {"properties":{"a":{}},"if":{"properties":{"a":{}}},"then":{"properties":{"b":{}}},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1,"b":2} => True/0; the anyOf and allOf equivalents also => True/0; an if/else pair where else is taken also => True/0. A FAILING anyOf branch does not annotate, but a later matching branch does. not does NOT annotate: {"not":{"properties":{"zz":{"type":"number"}}},"properties":{"a":{}},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1,"b":2} => 2. unevaluatedItems behaves the same and yields 1 error; note {"anyOf":[{"prefixItems":[{},{},{}]}],"unevaluatedItems":false} on [1,2,3] => False/1 under 2019-09 (prefixItems is not a keyword there, so no annotation) but True/0 under 2020-12.

PER-DRAFT KEYWORD AVAILABILITY (an absent keyword is silently ignored => 0 errors, never a schema error). allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not: draft-04+. if/then/else: draft-07+. dependencies: draft-03 through draft-07 ONLY -- REMOVED in 2019-09/2020-12, where {"dependencies":{"a":["b","c"]}} on {"a":1} => True/0 while draft-03/4/6/7 give 2 (schema form likewise 2 vs 0). dependentSchemas/dependentRequired: 2019-09+ only (2 there, 0 in draft<=7). contains: draft-06+ (draft-03/04 ignore). minContains/maxContains: 2019-09+ (draft-07 ignores, so {"contains":{"type":"number"},"maxContains":1} on [1,2,3] => True/0 in draft-07 but False/1 in 2019-09+). propertyNames: draft-06+ (2 errors for a 2-failing subschema; 0 in draft-03/04). const: draft-06+. prefixItems: 2020-12 ONLY -- unknown elsewhere, so {"prefixItems":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"string"}]} on [1,2] is True/0 for draft-03..2019-09 and False/2 for 2020-12. items as an ARRAY (tuple form) plus additionalItems: draft-04..draft-07. items:false on [1,2]: draft-07 DESCENDS per item => 2 errors; 2020-12 emits ONE aggregate error => 1. Boolean subschemas work inside combinators in EVERY draft including draft-04 ({"allOf":[true,false,false]} => 2 under Draft4Validator). Apart from the availability differences here and the $ref-sibling rule, draft-04 through 2020-12 count identically for allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not.

DRAFT-03 (the big special case). Draft3Validator has NO allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if, then, else, const, contains, propertyNames, prefixItems, dependentSchemas, dependentRequired -- all silently ignored, so a pure-combinator schema is vacuously valid. Analogs: extends DESCENDS and accepts a single schema OR an array of schemas ({"extends":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}} => 2; {"extends":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1},{"type":"number"}]} => 3; nested {"extends":{"extends":{2 failing}}} => 2; {"extends":[{"extends":{"minLength":9}},{"maxLength":1}]} => 2; {"extends":[]} => True/0; {"extends":{}} => True/0; {"extends":true} CRASHES). disallow COLLAPSES to exactly 1 ({"disallow":"string"} => 1, {"disallow":"any"} => 1, {"disallow":["string","number"]} => 1, {"disallow":[{"type":"object"}]} on {} => 1) and PASSES when its subschemas fail ({"disallow":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]} on "ab" => True/0); {"disallow":[]} => True/0. Draft-03 type given an array is the anyOf analog and COLLAPSES to 1 ({"type":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]} => 1; {"type":[]} => 1; mixed strings and schemas: {"type":[{"minLength":1},"number"]} => True/0, {"type":["number",{"minLength":9}]} => 1). Draft-03 required is a BOOLEAN inside each property schema, one error per missing required property ({"properties":{"a":{"required":true},"b":{"required":true}}} on {} => 2), and combines with extends ({"properties":{"a":{"required":true}},"extends":{"properties":{"b":{"required":true}}}} => 2). Draft-03 IGNORES draft-04-style {"required":["a","b"]} => True/0. divisibleBy is draft-03's multipleOf => 1. extends is draft-03 ONLY -- draft-04/06/07/2020-12 ignore it => True/0.

JAVASCRIPT-REIMPLEMENTER TRAPS (Python semantics leaking through). (1) STRING LENGTH IS CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 units: U+1D11E has length 1, so {"allOf":[{"maxLength":1}]} => True/0 and {"allOf":[{"minLength":2}]} => 1; two emoji have length 2 so {"maxLength":2} passes; a JS .length implementation gets all of these backwards. But combining marks DO count separately: "e"+U+0301 has length 2, so {"maxLength":1} => 1 error. {"propertyNames":{"allOf":[{"maxLength":1}]}} on an emoji key => True/0. (2) REGEX IS PYTHON re.search, NOT JS RegExp: pattern is a SEARCH not a full match ({"pattern":"b"} on "abc" => valid, {"pattern":"^b"} => 1). Python $ matches BEFORE a trailing newline, so {"pattern":"^a$"} on "a\n" => True/0 (JS would fail) and {"not":{"pattern":"^a$"}} on "a\n" => 1. \d and \w are UNICODE-aware: Arabic-Indic digit U+0663 matches "^\\d$" => True/0; "e"+U+0301 matches "^\\w$" => True/0. Python-only syntax works: inline flags (?i)abc matches "ABC"; \Z is supported; named groups (?P<x>a) are supported -- all three THROW in JS RegExp. "." matches an astral char as one unit: "^.$" matches an emoji => True/0. An INVALID regex like {"pattern":"["} CRASHES (exit 1). Overlapping patternProperties both apply: {"patternProperties":{"^a":{"type":"number"},"X$":{"type":"number"}}} on {"aX":"s","aY":"s"} => 3. (3) BOOLEANS ARE NOT NUMBERS despite Python bool<:int -- jsonschema unbools explicitly: true is neither "integer" nor "number" (1 error each); {"oneOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"boolean"}]} => True/0 for both true and 1; {"enum":[1]} rejects true and {"enum":[true]} rejects 1; {"const":1} rejects true and {"const":true} rejects 1; {"const":[true]} rejects [1]; uniqueItems treats them as DISTINCT ([true,1] unique, [0,false] unique, but [1,1.0,true] => 1 error because 1 and 1.0 collide). (4) 1 vs 1.0: numerically EQUAL for const/enum/uniqueItems ({"oneOf":[{"const":1},{"const":1.0}]} => 1 error from TWO matches, for both instance 1 and instance 1.0; {"oneOf":[{"const":1e2},{"const":100}]} on 100 => 1; [1,1.0] fails uniqueItems; {"const":{"a":1.0}} matches {"a":1}). But type:"integer" DIFFERS BY DRAFT: 1.0 is NOT an integer in draft-03/draft-04 but IS in draft-06+ (so {"oneOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"number"}]} on 1.0 => True/0 in draft-04 and False/1 in draft-06+ -- an actual validity flip). -0.0 and 1e2 are integers in draft-06+. (5) -0: JSON -0 parses to Python int 0, so {"const":-0} matches 0, {"oneOf":[{"const":0},{"const":-0}]} => 1 error (two matches), and [0,-0] FAILS uniqueItems. (6) FLOAT PRECISION: multipleOf uses float division, so {"multipleOf":0.1} on 0.3 FAILS (1 error) while {"multipleOf":0.0001} on 0.0075 and {"multipleOf":1.5} on 4.5 pass; {"multipleOf":1e-308} on 1e308 fails. Arbitrary-precision integers work: 12345678901234567890123 satisfies {"type":"integer"} and {"multipleOf":1}. 1e400 parses to float inf and satisfies {"type":"number"}. (7) OBJECT KEYS: duplicate JSON keys -> LAST wins ({"a":1,"a":2} matches {"properties":{"a":{"const":2}}}). Insertion order never changes error COUNTS. Deep equality is order-insensitive for objects ({"const":{"b":2,"a":1}} matches {"a":1,"b":2}) but order-SENSITIVE for arrays ({"enum":[[2,1],[1,2]]} matches [1,2] only via the second entry). (8) TYPE-INAPPLICABLE KEYWORDS ARE NO-OPS, silently reducing counts: {"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0},{"pattern":"^z"}]} on the NUMBER 1 => True/0; {"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"minItems":9},{"maxItems":0}]} on [1,2,3] => 2 (minLength skipped); {"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"type":"string"}]} on null => 1; {"properties":{"x":{"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"minLength":9}]}}} with x=1 => ONE error, not two. (9) format is NOT asserted by default: {"allOf":[{"format":"email"},{"format":"date"}]} on "zz" => True/0. (10) Unknown keywords and $comment are ignored without error.

contains DETAIL. Collapses to 1. Empty array with any contains => 1. {"contains":false} on [] => 1. {"contains":true} on [1] => True/0. A NON-ARRAY instance makes contains a no-op ({"contains":{"type":"number"}} on "a" => True/0). minContains/maxContains each add their own single error when violated ([1,2,3] with maxContains:1 => 1; minContains:5 => 1; minContains:2,maxContains:2 => 1). {"contains":{"type":"number"},"minContains":0} on [] => True/0. contains and a sibling items both fire: {"contains":{allOf 2 failing},"items":{allOf 2 failing}} on ["a","a"] => 5 (1 + 4).

CRASH MATRIX (exit=1, empty stdout). For allOf/anyOf/oneOf the value is iterated and each element handed to the schema machinery. NON-CRASHING degenerate values are exactly the EMPTY ITERABLES "" and {}: {"allOf":""} and {"allOf":{}} => True/0 (vacuous), while {"anyOf":""}, {"anyOf":{}}, {"oneOf":""}, {"oneOf":{}} => False/1 (nothing matched), mirroring {"allOf":[]} => True/0 vs {"anyOf":[]}/{"oneOf":[]} => False/1. EVERYTHING ELSE CRASHES: non-empty strings ({"allOf":"x"}, {"allOf":"ab"} -- iterating yields chars, AttributeError 'str' has no attribute 'get'), non-empty objects ({"allOf":{"type":"number"}}, {"allOf":{"a":{...}}}, {"allOf":{"":{}}} -- iterating yields keys), and all non-iterables (0, 1.5, null, true, false). Bad ELEMENTS crash too: {"allOf":[null]}, {"allOf":[1]}, {"allOf":[[]]}, {"allOf":[[{...}]]}, {"anyOf":[[]]}. Because anyOf short-circuits, a bad element AFTER a matching branch is never reached (no crash); oneOf always scans the rest, so it always crashes. For not, ONLY a dict or bool is legal: {"not":{}} => 1, {"not":true} => 1, {"not":false} => 0, while {"not":[]}, {"not":""}, {"not":"x"}, {"not":0}, {"not":1.5}, {"not":null}, {"not":[{...}]} ALL CRASH -- note {"not":[]} and {"not":""} crash even though empty. Same for if: {"if":{}}, {"if":true}, {"if":false} are fine; {"if":[]}, {"if":""}, {"if":"x"}, {"if":0}, {"if":null} crash. contains and propertyNames crash on null/1/[]/"" values. Other crashes: {"pattern":"["} (invalid regex), {"$schema":7}, draft-03 {"extends":true}, unresolvable $ref pointers (including inside anyOf), remote http $ref, and 2019-09 $recursiveRef without $id. Malformed JSON in either --a or --b also crashes the same way.
gotchas: The prior report's vector count (193) was wrong (file had 146) and several cited vectors did not exist. Its claim that additionalProperties DESCENDS is WRONG: additionalProperties DESCENDS only when its value is a SCHEMA; additionalProperties:false emits exactly ONE aggregate error no matter how many extra properties (3 extras => 1 error). Same for 2020-12 items:false and draft-07 additionalItems:false.

BIGGEST MISS: $ref SIBLING KEYWORDS. In Draft4/6/7 all keywords sibling to $ref are IGNORED; in 2019-09/2020-12 they are applied. {"$ref":"#/X/a","minLength":9,"maxLength":0} where the ref target also fails => 1 error under draft-4/6/7 but 3 under 2019-09/2020-12. Same inside allOf: 1 vs 2.

anyOf SHORT-CIRCUITS on the first matching branch but oneOf NEVER does (it must scan every branch to count matches). Observable: {"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},null]} on "a" is VALID/0, but {"oneOf":[{"type":"string"},null]} on "a" CRASHES with exit=1. allOf never short-circuits either.

allOf/then/else/properties/patternProperties/items/prefixItems/propertyNames/$ref/dependentSchemas DESCEND (N child errors => N top-level errors, multiplying through chains). anyOf/oneOf/not/contains/minContains/maxContains/draft-03 disallow/draft-03 array-type COLLAPSE to exactly 1. A single COLLAPSE keyword anywhere on the path caps that whole subtree at 1 error.
propertyNames DESCENDS (not collapses) and runs per key: {"propertyNames":{"allOf":[{"maxLength":0},{"pattern":"^z"}]}} on a 2-key object => 4 errors. It is draft-06+; draft-03/04 ignore it entirely.

Empty combinator values diverge: {"allOf":[]} / {"allOf":""} / {"allOf":{}} => VALID/0, but {"anyOf":[]} / {"anyOf":""} / {"anyOf":{}} / {"oneOf":[]} / {"oneOf":{}} => INVALID with exactly 1 error. Any OTHER non-array value (non-empty string, non-empty object, 0, 1.5, null, true, false) CRASHES with exit=1 and empty stdout.
oneOf yields exactly 1 error for BOTH failure modes -- 0 matches and 2+ matches (4 branches with 3 matches => 1). Never emit one error per extra match.

then/else DESCEND: a then-branch with 3 failing keywords produces 3 TOP-LEVEL errors, not 1. And then/else WITHOUT a sibling `if` are completely ignored (0 errors); `if` alone with no then/else never errors even when it fails.
if/then/else are LAZY: {"if":{"type":"number"},"then":null} on a string is VALID/0, but {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":null} CRASHES. Only the taken branch is ever touched.
